source.title: Building the System
source.summary: What an Islamic monetary system would look like, not at the bank level, but at the system level. Principles, obstacles, and the path forward.
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: Gold dinar revival proposals sound appealing but face practical limitations. This episode moves beyond nostalgia to ask what a modern Islamic monetary system would actually require: five design principles for an Islamic monetary authority, the question of OIC monetary cooperation, and why governance is the binding constraint, not monetary design. The principles exist, the capital exists, the technology exists, and the need is real. But building institutions requires the hardest thing of all: trust between governments that have rarely cooperated at this level.
